Documentation and History: Certificate from W. E. Hill & Son, London dated 20th September 1948. A Letter from W. E. Hill & Sons dated 3rd June 1948 giving the history of the violin (see below). An extract from a letter from Miss Atherstone dated 30th March 1876. A letter from Edward Remery dated 15th September 1887 from Grahams-town, South Africa, addressed to Dr. Guyton Atherstone. A letter from Carl Walther dated 14th July 1888 also from Grahamstown and addressed to Mr. Bidwell. A letter from M. E. Atherstone dated 16th November 1889 and addressed to The Hon. W. G. Atherstone, M.D. The text of the letter from A. Phillips Hill reads as follows: - “At about the middle of the last century, it was in the hands of a Mr. Goding of Belgrave Square, London who possessed an important collection of Italian instruments. At that time this violin was attributed to Joseph Guarnerius and was said to have been called ‘The Giant’ by Paganini. There is no documentary evidence of this and we incline to the opinion that that attribution was given to it for some ulterior motive by a dealer of those times who was responsible for having somewhat altered the sound holes to resemble those of Joseph Guarnerius. It later passed into the hands of a Dr. Atherstone who emigrated to South Africa. After his decease it remained in the possession of his widow for many years and was then sold to a Mr. Darter. The instrument was brought back to this country by the descendants of the last named and sold to one of our colleagues in London, from whom it now passes into your possession. This violin was known to the Hungarian player Edouard Remenyi of Budapest who in a letter dated 1887, refers to it as having a tone of exceptional volume from which feature it had no doubt been named ‘The Giant’”. (See Colour Illustration and detail of the head)
